title: Fallen Survey Line
description: A surviving foot and three split shaft drums along one fall line, ending in a broken cushion capital.

review.notes: Round 2, checked against the round-1 points. The convex ribs are gone, but the drums are now faceted boxy blocks with stair-stepped notches cut into one face, so the row reads as stepped boulders or stair fragments, not fallen column drums (hero, closeup_upper, closeup_base). No capital is recognisable: the right piece is a scalloped disc, the left a flat slab with a wavy top. The pieces stand in a straight row on edge like a fence rather than lying along a fall line. Material is clean white with blotchy grey smudges. Fix: round drums (true cylinders) with concave Doric flutes and sharp arrises, lying on their sides at varied angles, half sunk into the turf, decreasing in size along a fall line; one profiled broken capital (echinus plus abacus) at the end; fracture faces as large planes with secondary chips; grime and lichen on the down side and where they touch the ground.
